Perform Friedman Test and Nemenyi Post-Hoc Analysis with Output Saving

friedman.nemenyi.new.Rd

This function performs a Friedman test to evaluate statistically significant differences among multiple methods. If significant differences are detected, a Nemenyi post-hoc test is applied. The function automatically generates and saves summary statistics, a Critical Difference (CD) plot, a p-values plot, and CSV files with the results.

friedman.nemenyi.new(
  data,
  save,
  measure.name,
  width = 7,
  height = 5,
  cex = 1.2,
  device = c("pdf", "png"),
  dpi = 150
)

Arguments

data

A data frame where each row represents a method and each column represents an observation or measurement.

save

A character string specifying the directory where output files will be saved.

measure.name

A character string used as the base name for all output files.

width

Numeric value specifying the width of the output plots (in inches).

height

Numeric value specifying the height of the output plots (in inches).

cex

Numeric value controlling the size of text elements in the plots.

device

Character string indicating the graphics device to be used for the plots. Possible values are "pdf" (vector graphics, default) and "png" (raster graphics).

dpi

Numeric value specifying the resolution (dots per inch) for PNG output. This parameter is only used when device = "png".

Value

A data frame with the following columns:

ChiSquare

Chi-square statistic from the Friedman test.

pValue

P-value associated with the Friedman test.

Method

Name of the statistical test used.

CriticalDifference

Critical Difference value from the Nemenyi test.

Result

Textual interpretation of statistical significance.

Details

The output plots can be generated either as vector-based PDF files or as rasterized PNG images. Using PNG is recommended when dealing with a large number of methods, as it significantly reduces file size and improves compilation performance in LaTeX/Overleaf environments.

The function generates the following output files:

  • A CSV file containing the Friedman test statistics.

  • A CSV file containing the Nemenyi post-hoc difference matrix.

  • A Critical Difference (CD) plot comparing the average ranks of the methods.

  • A p-values plot visualizing pairwise post-hoc comparisons.

When device = "pdf", plots are saved as vector graphics using useDingbats = FALSE to ensure compatibility with LaTeX compilers. When device = "png", plots are rasterized at the specified resolution, producing significantly smaller files for complex CD plots.

See also

friedmanTest, nemenyiTest, plotCD, plotPvalues

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Example usage with PNG output (recommended for Overleaf)
result <- friedman.nemenyi.new(
  data = my_data,
  save = "output_dir",
  measure.name = "my_measure",
  width = 14,
  height = 7,
  cex = 2,
  device = "png",
  dpi = 150
)

# Example usage with PDF output
result <- friedman.nemenyi.new(
  data = my_data,
  save = "output_dir",
  measure.name = "my_measure"
)
} # }
